name: Enlarging an existing throat (r_0 -> r_1 on already nontrivial topology) is a metric change, not a topology change, so Geroch/Tipler/Borde say nothing about it

source.located: The claim is the tree's own reading of the SCOPE of Geroch (J. Math. Phys. 8, 782, 1967), Tipler (Ann. Phys. 108, 1, 1977) and Borde (arXiv:gr-qc/9406053v1, 1994). Borde is READ at source (cached arXiv v1 full text, src/gr-qc_9406053.txt, md5 17c67ada52d92fc44065246ef92fee8c): definitions sec. published_statement: There is no published statement of the tree's sentence. What the source states (Borde gr-qc/9406053v1, verbatim): Theorem 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' Corollary: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M can be foliated by spacelike surfaces, with S1 as the first surface in the foliation and S2 as the last. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1]'. Theorem 3 (dim >= 3, null generic condition (i), half-integral null convergence condition (ii)): 'Then M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1], and S1 and S2 are connected.' Reinhart/Sorkin as quoted: 'If n is even, then M admits such a field if chi(M) = 0'; Misner/Geroch procedure: 'If N = M#V, then chi(N) = chi(M) + chi(V) - 2', 'CP2 ... with chi = 3'. Scope: 'The results in the rest of this paper all deal with causally compact interpolating spacetimes ... where the timelike component T of dM is empty, or, if non-empty, where M is a causally compact region of a larger, externally simple spacetime'. Tipler (restated, Borde IX.A): 'if topology change occurs via a non-compact interpolating spacetime, then it contains (under some mild additional assumptions) a singularity ... or a point at infinity.' The operative point: every conclusion is about the INTERPOLATING MANIFOLD M (product or not), not about a pair of endpoint topologies.
published_hypotheses: Borde Thm 1 / Geroch: M is an interpolating spacetime -- connected smooth manifold, boundary S1 u S2 (u compact timelike tube T), smooth everywhere non-degenerate Lorentz metric with S1, S2 spacelike [Borde II.A, lines 200-265]
causally compact (closure of I(p) compact for all p; automatic for compact M); for open universes, M is the causally compact region of an externally simple spacetime [Borde lines 1160-1210]
NO field equation, NO energy condition, NO completeness assumption in Thm 1 [Borde IX]
Thm 3 adds: dimension >= 3, null generic condition (i), half-integral null convergence condition (ii)
Tipler Thm 5 (restated): closed-universe case, NON-compact interpolating spacetime, topology change occurs, 'some mild additional assumptions' (unnamed; Tipler NOT READ)

The theorems' antecedent is NOT 'topology change'; their conclusion is 'M = S1 x [0,1]'. They therefore constrain every non-product interpolating M -- including M whose two ends are the SAME manifold -- and are silent (conclusion already true) exactly when M is a product.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED -- the product hypothesis, replaced by an endpoint boolean. create.py:235-236 is_topology_change(initial_nontrivial, final_nontrivial) = (initial != final); create.py:239-245 enlarging_is_topology_change() = is_topology_change(True, True) = False and theorems_apply_to_enlargement() returns it. Borde's Theorems 1 and 3 conclude 'M diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1]', a statement about the interpolating manifold. Computed here (C4): M = (Sigma x I) # (S1xS3) # CP2 # CP2, Sigma = S1xS2, has identical NONTRIVIAL ends, chi(M) = 0 (so a Lorentz metric with both ends spacelike exists, by the Reinhart condition Borde quotes), and b1(M) = 2 != b1(Sigma x I) = 1, so M is not a product and Theorem 1 forces a CTC -- while the tree's predicate returns 'no topology change'. z3 (C5b) unsat with vacuity guard. The sufficient condition for the theorems to be silent is 'M = Sigma x [0,1]' (a metric family on a FIXED manifold), not 'nontrivial before and after'.

C3: R^3#(S1xS2) (b1=1) -> R^3#2(S1xS2) (b1=2) is a genuine topology change (adding a second handle) on which Geroch/Borde apply in full, but is_topology_change(True, True) = False. The ENLARGEMENT function never passes this case, so the defect is in the general predicate, not in the one call the tree makes.

IMPLICIT, NOW NAMED -- r(t) > 0 throughout the enlargement. C1: in the explicit family the only degeneration is at a = 0, where the throat sphere collapses (R(0) = 0) -- the pinch-off, which IS a topology change. 'From r_0 to r_1' (create.py:106, 240) carries it only implicitly; an enlargement path that passes through a pinch is not a metric change.

IMPLICIT, NOW NAMED -- the non-degenerate smooth Lorentz metric on the whole region (as for the CREATE side; see audit geroch-1967-topology-change). On a product with a non-degenerate metric, C1 shows g^{tt} = -1 so t is a time function and no CTC exists: the theorems' conclusion holds trivially.

PHRASING (not an error) -- create.py:102 'Every theorem above is about TOPOLOGY CHANGE' / create.py:104 'NONE OF THIS APPLIES'. Borde's Theorem 1 has no topology-change antecedent; it APPLIES to an enlargement spacetime and returns 'M is a product', which is already true (C5a sat). Its effect is 'imposes nothing', which is what the tree means; Theorem 3's and Tipler Thm 5's hypotheses do include topology change (Borde's abstract: 'causally compact topology-changing spacetimes').

ADDED (beyond the source, unscoped) -- create.py:106 'Permitted.' and create.py:107-108 'Every instrument this tree has built for the CONTAIN problem applies to it unmodified.' The topology-change theorems being silent does not make enlargement permitted by GR: C2 reproduces, for an explicit enlargement family, that NEC must fail at Hayward's dynamic mouth (z3: temporal mouth with G_++ >= 0 unsat), as Hayward 0903.5438 ('The null energy condition must be violated at a wormhole mouth') and Hochberg-Visser gr-qc/9802048 state. Hochberg-Visser also show 'time-dependent wormholes have two throats, one for each direction ... the two throats coalesce only for the case of a static wormhole' -- so static CONTAIN instruments apply to an enlargement only at its static endpoints, not 'unmodified' during it. This is a scope note on the 'Permitted' sentence; the tree's D24/ledger wording ('those theorems say nothing about') is the narrower, correct one.

NAMED IN THE TREE, SHARPENED BY THE LITERATURE -- create.py:103 'primordial, inherited, a relic'. Hayward gr-qc/9805019 p.4: 'astrophysical black holes, presumably formed by gravitational collapse, are not expected to have the right topology for global traversibility. Black holes formed by quantum fluctuations, either in the early universe or by some hypothetical quantum engineering, may well have wormhole topology'. The provenance hypothesis is load-bearing: an object whose own history was a topology change inherits Geroch's constraint in its past.

lacked_data: No numerical datum enters: the result is kinematic (differential topology plus causal structure), so there is no measured quantity whose update could move it, and M's hypothesis 'previous physicists lacked certain data' has no purchase on the theorem itself -- evidence: Borde Thm 1 is 'purely kinematical' (Borde IX, READ) and C1/C5 re-derive the silence on a product exactly. What changed after 1967/1977/1994 is not data but LITERATURE on the dynamical side: Hochberg-Visser 1998 and Hayward 1999/2009 supply the dynamic-throat theory (two throats, NEC at the mouth, enlargement by negative energy) that neither Geroch nor Tipler addressed. That later work does not change the theorems' conclusion; it changes what 'permitted' can mean for enlargement (C2). The only empirical input the ROUTE depends on -- whether any pre-existing nontrivial spatial topology exists -- is unmeasured (create.py ROUTE_COST 'nobody has ever observed one'); Hayward 1999 notes collapse-formed black holes lack it. Having that datum would change whether the route has an object, not whether the theorems are silent on it.
grade_evidence: STANDS for the class the prose sentence describes: an enlargement realised as a family of non-degenerate metrics on a FIXED spatial manifold with the throat radius kept > 0 gives a product interpolating spacetime (C1: t is a time function, throat exists for all a > 0), on which Borde's Theorems 1 and 3 (and Geroch's, as restated) conclude only what is already true (C5a) and Tipler Thm 5's topology-change antecedent fails; Borde READ at source. NARROWED because the tree's ENCODING and its dependent class are wider than that: (1) create.py:235-245 decides 'the theorems apply' from two endpoint booleans; C4 computes a Lorentzian, non-product cobordism with IDENTICAL nontrivial ends (chi = 0; b1 2 vs 1) on which Theorem 1 forces a CTC while the predicate says 'no topology change' (z3 C5b unsat, vacuity-guarded); C3 shows the one-bit 'nontrivial' misses 1 -> 2 handles. (2) specthm.py:1666-1669 W-enlarge has hyps [] -- the product / fixed-manifold / r > 0 hypotheses on which silence rests are unnamed there and at ledger.py:632-635. (3) create.py:106-108 'Permitted ... applies unmodified' goes beyond what silence of these theorems gives: C2 reproduces NEC violation at a temporal dynamic mouth for the enlargement family, and Hochberg-Visser show a dynamic wormhole has two throats. Not WRONG: no counterexample touches the fixed-manifold enlargement the tree actually means; the counterexamples are to the general predicate and the unscoped class. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters. Not OPEN: Borde is read and the claim is checked; only Geroch 1967 and Tipler 1977 at source remain NAMED-NOT-READ, which bounds the source status, not the grade.
what_would_change_the_grade: -> STANDS if the tree states the operative hypothesis where the flag is computed and consumed: is_topology_change keyed on the interpolating manifold being a product (Sigma x [0,1], a metric family on a fixed manifold with r > 0 throughout) rather than on two booleans, and W-enlarge / D24 carrying that hypothesis by name; and 'Permitted' scoped to 'not forbidden by the topology-change theorems' (NEC at the dynamic mouth still owed). -> WRONG only if an enlargement on a FIXED manifold with non-degenerate metric were shown to fall under Geroch/Borde/Tipler -- C1/C5a show it cannot for Theorem 1; reading Tipler 1977 at source could in principle reveal a Theorem-5 antecedent weaker than 'topology change', which would be recorded. -> OPEN would not apply unless Borde's text were found to misstate Theorem 1 relative to a later version (v1 is what was read).
